transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-07-30
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Jamal Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Sinha (Redwood DA) — Maya Chen (AtlasRetail Lead ML Eng), Rohit Patel (SRE), Elena Gomez (PM), Samir Bose (Security)

---
[00:00] Lena: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um we'll go for about 50 minutes, quick orientation on the SDKs and auth flows and then leave time for infra/security questions. any scheduling issues?
[00:16] Maya: all good, thanks Lena. we've got a few folks from infra and security on to make sure we can hit our compliance bar.
[00:23] Lena: perfect. jamal will run through the code demos, priya's got some notes on optimize best practices. quick note — i'll drop the quickstart repo and a sandbox key after this call.
[00:33] Jamal: cool, i'll start with the python quickstart, then show the ts client and how to wire auth. heads up — the transcript might show "Reedwood" a couple times cause captions likes that.
[00:45] [00:45] Jamal: ok, so the gist for python is pip install redwood-client, set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your env, and then you can call client.generate(...) — in our demo the sample uses generation endpoint with model redwood-7b-quant, you can also pass streaming=true for chunked responses.
[01:10] Rohit: quick Q — how do you recommend storing the api key for CI? we use GitHub Actions and don't want accidental leaks.
[01:18] Jamal: yep, good call. recommended pattern: store the key in your org secrets (GH Actions secrets), then reference as env var REDWOOD_API_KEY in the workflow. for ephemeral developer keys use the console and revoke when needed. also we support scoped keys in Dedicated plans.
[01:34] Samir: how do keys map to audits? we need the token-level tracing/audit logs for compliance.
[01:39] Priya: we have token-level request logs in the console for hosted & dedicated, plus optional audit export to your SIEM. we'll share the security checklist with exact retention and export options.
[01:52] [02:00] Jamal: switching to TypeScript quickstart — npm i @redwood/inference (note: package name in demo might be slightly different in repo), then use const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); and client.chat.create(...) — we show both the sync and streaming patterns.
[02:25] Maya: can you show local dev flow? we typically want offline dev for prompt iteration.
[02:30] Jamal: yep — locally you set REDWOOD_API_KEY in your .env, use direnv or similar. for offline/mock testing we recommend our sandbox with deterministic responses or you can run a lightweight local mock that returns canned outputs. important: don't check .env into git.
[02:48] Lena: one pattern we've seen work well is per-developer keys in the console, and a system key scoped to CI with limited permissions so you can rotate independently.
[03:05] [03:05] Elena: about SSO — we use Okta and want SAML for console access, not individual user passwords.
[03:12] Lena: absolutely — we support SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning. for RBAC you can map Okta groups to roles in the Console.
[03:25] Samir: data residency: some of our checkout logs must stay in eu-west, do you support region pinning?
[03:31] Priya: for Hosted we have region options; for Dedicated or Private you can pin to a region or run in your VPC. we'll include region options in the security doc.
[03:45] [04:00] Jamal: demo time — i'm going to share my screen and walk through the repo. first file, examples/python_quickstart.py — note there's a small comment about the prompt templates and using params vs f-strings to avoid injection.
[04:21] [04:30] Jamal: typing a quick run: client.generate(model='redwood-7b-quant', prompt=prompt, max_tokens=256) — results come back with choices[0].text. small thing: some transcripts might show 'kv cash' instead of KV cache, and sometimes model names get scrambled.
[04:55] Maya: are there example prompts or prompt sets you recommend for classification vs generation?
[05:02] Priya: yes — we have prompt libraries in the repo: classification.md, summarization.md. also Optimize will surface guardrails and regression tests for your prompt sets.
[05:20] [06:00] Jamal: switching to CI example — here's a GitHub Actions snippet: name: run-inference-test, uses: actions/checkout, run: python -m pytest — env: REDWOOD_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.REDWOOD_API_KEY }}. for node we set process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY.
[06:28] Rohit: do you recommend separate prod keys vs staging keys?
[06:33] Lena: yes — separate keys, separate projects in the Console. prod keys should be more restricted and rotated via KMS integration.
[06:45] Samir: can we integrate with our KMS/HSM for key management?
[06:50] Priya: on Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM and bring-your-own-key; for Hosted we support envelope encryption and integration with cloud KMS for key wrapping. we'll share the KMS integration doc.
[07:10] [08:00] Jamal: now a quick TS snippet showing streaming and handling partial tokens — common pitfall is not handling partial json in structured responses, we suggest using the provided JSON schema helper in the client that will buffer tokens until valid JSON.
[08:30] Maya: that's helpful — we do a lot of structured output for product descriptions, so robust parsing is key.
[08:40] Jamal: worth noting: Optimize has configuration suggestions for batching and quantization profiles per workload. for example high throughput chat vs single inference transforms have different recommended batch sizes and kv cache settings.
[09:02] Elena: can you give a rough delta on cost if we enable caching vs not?
[09:08] Priya: it's workload dependent, but caching prefixes can reduce token throughput by 20-60% for repeated contexts. we'll run a quick estimate in the POC with your histograms.
[09:20] [10:00] Jamal: next, console demo — quick tour: projects, keys, model catalog, logs, and the Optimize tab where you can see suggestion cards. you can pin model versions and do canary rollouts from the console.
[10:30] Rohit: is there an API you can call to rotate keys or automate rollouts?
[10:36] Lena: yes, everything's also exposed via the REST/HTTP API so platform teams can script provisioning and rollouts.
[10:45] Samir: what about private deployment — we have air-gapped environments for payment flows.
[10:51] Priya: Private supports air-gapped on-prem installs; there's a longer onboarding for compliance but it's an option. dedicated will also give you isolated GPU pools without full on-prem.
[11:12] [12:00] Jamal: small demo hiccup — my terminal font made the code wrap weirdly sorry. moving on, here's the quickstart README link: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstarts (demo note: link will be in followup email).
[12:29] Maya: can you share the sample eval harness? we want to run regression tests on prompt changes.
[12:35] Priya: yes — we have an evals folder with unit test style harness and CSV reporting; Optimize can also integrate those and trigger regression alerts.
[12:50] [14:00] Maya: timeline question — we'd like a short POC with 2-3 endpoints and perf targets inside 3 weeks, is that realistic?
[14:07] Lena: yes, we typically do a 3-week POC — week 1 onboarding & baseline tests, week 2 integration + perf tuning, week 3 validation and handover. we'll scope details in the follow-up.
[14:25] Rohit: on perf, what's the expected latency for models like redwood-7b-quant on hosted vs dedicated?
[14:31] Jamal: hosted median token latency is usually in the 50-150ms range for that class depending on sequence length; dedicated will give more predictable tail latency and higher throughput. we'll run your sample traces to provide realistic numbers.
[14:50] [16:00] Jamal: security deep dive — Samir can you share specific compliance controls you need?
[16:06] Samir: we need SOC2 type II evidence, SAML SSO, audit logs, RBAC, and data residency guarantees. also pen test report if available.
[16:20] Priya: we'll attach SOC2 and pen test summaries; private/dedicated have added contractual SLAs.
[16:32] Lena: we'll also send the threat model and a short handbook on how we handle data in transit and at rest.
[16:45] [18:00] Maya: one last technical — do you have a recommended strategy for prompt templating across teams to avoid duplication and drift?
[18:07] Jamal: yes, keep templates in a central repo, use the SDK's template loader with param substitution, and run regular evals. Optimize can show regressions when prompt changes reduce quality.
[18:25] [20:00] Elena: any known gotchas migrating from our current self-hosted LLM infra?
[20:07] Jamal: common ones: mismatch in tokenization, prompt length distribution differences, and missing KV cache optimizations. we usually run a calibration step to pick quantization and batch tuning.
[20:30] Rohit: would Redwood support a side-by-side test while we keep current infra in prod?
[20:36] Lena: absolutely — traffic shadowing and canary is supported so you can compare outputs and latency without impacting prod traffic.
[21:00] [24:00] Jamal: sharing a couple of links in chat: quickstart repo, security checklist, and a sample GH Actions snippet.
[24:20] Maya: thanks — please also share example dashboards for cost breakdown.
[24:28] Priya: will do, console has token-level cost breakdowns per-route and per-model which we'll include screenshots of.
[24:50] [28:00] Jamal: wrapping up code notes — for TypeScript, watch out for the streaming callback signature differences between node runtimes, we provide polyfills in the client.
[28:30] Lena: recap: we'll send sandbox credentials, quickstart links, security docs (SOC2, KMS guide), and a POC scoping doc. jamal to prep CI secrets how-to.
[28:52] Maya: sounds good.
[29:00] [32:00] Samir: one minor question — do you grade or flag hallucinations? we need an SLA on accuracy for some endpoints.
[32:06] Priya: we provide quality monitoring and can set up alerts tied to evaluation sets; SLA on accuracy is something we can define in POC and monitor.
[32:20] Rohit: are there any sample cost estimates for our expected qps?
[32:25] Lena: with your approximate qps (Maya gave 10 rps peak) we can send a cost model; Optimize will give suggestions to shave costs with batching and caching.
[32:40] [36:00] Jamal: final question from my side — what language runtimes are you standardizing on? python/node?
[36:06] Maya: python for model work, node for product microservices. so both major SDKs are critical.
[36:15] Jamal: great, that's aligned with the repo.
[36:30] [40:00] Lena: any blockers to move to POC?
[40:05] Elena: need security signoff and a POC SOW.
[40:10] Lena: we'll draft SOW and share; timeline target ok?
[40:18] Elena: yes, aiming to start first week of August.
[40:26] [44:00] Jamal: small wrap note — sometimes transcripts garble model names; example redwood-7b shows up as 'redwood 7 b' in captions. nothing to worry about.
[44:20] Maya: thanks everyone.
[44:30] [48:00] Lena: ok we'll follow up with artifacts. thanks for the time.
[48:10] Meeting ended.
